purpose: Cefuroxime axetil is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, sinus infections, throat infections, bronchitis, urinary tract infections, skin infections, and Lyme disease. It works only against bacteria and will not treat colds, flu, or other viral infections. Your doctor prescribed it to help your body fight off a specific bacterial infection.
how_it_works: This antibiotic works by attacking the outer wall that surrounds bacteria. Think of it like breaking down the protective shell that bacteria need to survive. Without that wall, the bacteria fall apart and die, helping your infection clear up.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach upset, and vomiting. Some people may notice a change in taste, especially with the tablet form. You might also get a headache or develop a mild skin rash.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or any other antibiotics, as you may also be allergic to this medication. Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you develop severe diarrhea, a bad rash, difficulty breathing, or swelling of your face or throat. Always finish the full course even if you feel better early, so the infection does not come back stronger.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 250 mg to 500 mg taken twice a day, depending on the type of infection. It is best taken with food to help your stomach tolerate it and to help your body absorb it better. Your doctor will tell you exactly how long to take it, but most courses last 5 to 10 days.
